Laṅkaka
alias Alaṅkāra, third son of Viśvāvarta, son of Manmatha; elder brother of Maṅkha, the minister of Jayasiṃha of Kashmir; a great grammarian an. Sāndhi-vigrahika of King Sussal of Kashmir (died in 1128 C. E.); flourished also during Sussala's son Jayasiṃha's time (1129-50 C. E.).
See Śrīkaṇṭhacarita of Maṅkha, III. 56-62. XXV. 15; also Rājataraṅgiṇī VIII. 2423 ff. Report p. 52.

Laṅkāvatārasūtra
or Saddharma laṅkāvatārasūtra or Ṣaṭtriṃśatsāhasra. Bud. Mahāyāna; belongs to Sūtrānta. One of the nine sacred books of Nepalese Buddhists in 10 Ch.. (contains 36000 v..)treats of a. imaginary philosophical disquisition between the Buddha with Rāvaṇa (ch. 1) an. Mahāmati (chs. 2-10); exists also in a Tibetan an. three Chinese versions.
See Wint. HIL. II. p. 283; also Levi, BMFJ. I. i. 49.
For a note, see S. C. Vidyabhushan, Laṅkāvatārasūtra, JRAS (1905) 831-37; also IA. Vol. XX. p. 87; also G. Tucci, IHQ. IV- 3. 1928. p.. 545-56. For a detailed study, see D. T. Suzuki, Studies in the Laṅkāvatārasūtra, London, 1930. p.. xxxii. 464; also published by Munshiram Manoharlal Pub. Pvt. Ltd., New Delhi, 1998.
On the Laṅkāvatasūtra an. Sāṅkhya, see J. W. Hauer, Das Laṅkāvatārasūtra und das Sāṅkhya (eine vorlaujige skizzeo), Stuttgart, 1927.
AMG. II. p. 237. AR. XX. p. 432. AS. p. 253. Br. Mus. 535. Cabaton 1. 95-96. Cambr. Uni. Bud. p. 27. Fasc. I. 95-96. Hod. Bud. 5. IO.7716 (Umāpatiśāstra). JBORS. XXIII. i. p. 53 (2 mss. ; inc.). National Libr. Nepal I. p. 71 (4 mss.). Kanjur Kyoto 775. Nanjio 176-¬77. Sendai 107. Suzuki, Otani 775.
